access.coverageNote: Stage 1 mapped all three entry points and both full questionnaire definitions. Stage 2 replayed the three baselines and ran 40 one-change experiments (22 women, 18 men). Stage 3 (independent check) replayed the baselines again, re-tested 11 key rules live, added the last untested men's options (specialist diagnosis, pattern B, skin condition, peanut and other-substance allergy) and two women's combinations. Every question option except delivery choices and the men's 'Other medications' allergy has now been replayed. Age, sex and the doctor's decision sit behind the account wall and were not tested.

questions.text: Almost done. Important information to read and confirm you agree and understand: Trying for a baby – Finasteride may affect male fertility while you are taking it. These changes are usually reversible after stopping treatment, but recovery may take several months. If you are planning to try for a baby, it is best not to use this or to stop it several months before trying to conceive. Depression – Some people have experienced severe depression when taking finasteride. Before taking finasteride, read and keep the finasteride patient cards and patient information leaflet within your pack and inform your doctor if you have any personal history of depression or suicidal thought. You should stop taking this medication immediately if you notice that your mood is affected and speak to your doctor. Finasteride and your prostate – Finasteride can lower the level of a prostate protein called PSA (prostate-specific antigen) in your blood. Because of this, it’s recommended that you see your GP for a prostate check (rectal examination) and a PSA blood test before starting treatment, and then at regular intervals while taking it. How often this is needed will depend on your age and personal risk factors. These checks help to detect any prostate problems, including prostate cancer, as early as possible. Sexual problems – If you experience decreased sex drive, difficulty having an erection or ejaculation problems on finasteride, you should contact your doctor for medical advice. This medication is prescribed for your own personal use – If you are requesting any follow-up medication, you confirm you are tolerating your treatment and any side effects experienced. Your answers are used to make medical decisions – Answer the questions honestly and as accurately as you can. Our doctors rely on this information to prescribe treatment safely. Missing or incorrect information can increase the risk of side effects or lead to serious risk to your health. In case of questions, please contact us. By continuing, you confirm that you have understood the information provided, especially around treatment options, side effects, and effectiveness.

engineSummary: Superdrug Online Doctor (Zava platform) runs no recommendation engine. Each service is a one-page medical questionnaire with show/hide follow-ups, followed by a product list the patient picks from; the doctor decides after account creation and payment. Men: the list is fixed (generic finasteride or Propecia in four pack sizes, or a £25 phone consultation). Sixteen one-change replays, including prostate cancer, breast cancer and finasteride allergy, never changed it; the only on-screen effects are warning texts (scalp symptoms, erection problems, advanced pattern E) and a photo upload that blocks the form for patterns A, E and 'none fits'. Women: a server-side product-rules call silently removes products by ingredient and suitability: Regaine for Women goes for high blood pressure, heart disease, non-pattern presentations and minoxidil/ethanol/propylene glycol allergy; Nourkrin for fish allergy; Alpecin for caffeine allergy. Removals add up: a woman allergic to minoxidil, fish and caffeine is left with only the phone consultation, with no message. Pregnancy changes nothing. No answer ever stops the patient before the account wall.
strengths: Trusted high-street brand; CQC-registered doctor service and GPhC-registered Superdrug pharmacies.
Very short: one page, no account until after product and delivery choice, prices shown up front.
Low generic finasteride price (£27 a month, £137 for six months) with free delivery or free store collection.
Women's list is filtered by ingredient allergies and minoxidil safety (blood pressure, heart, non-pattern loss) before the patient chooses, so unsuitable items never show.
Asks for photos when the chosen pattern does not look like typical male pattern loss, and sets realistic expectations for advanced loss.
Clear consent text on fertility, depression, PSA and sexual side effects.
weaknesses: Men's screen is not acted on: finasteride allergy, prostate or breast cancer, past low mood on finasteride and sudden loss all still show finasteride and Propecia with no answer-specific warning (only the general consent text); everything waits for the doctor after payment.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding do not remove Regaine for Women or show any warning, although the product should not be used then.
Removals for women are silent: no explanation of why a product disappeared or what to do instead.
Men are offered tablets only: no topical finasteride, no minoxidil (Regaine for Men is advertised but not in the flow), no oral minoxidil, no combinations.
No guidance on which product or pack to choose; no personalisation, no 'recommended' result.
No questions on mood or mental health, family history, age, or fertility plans for men; none on periods, menopause, contraception, PCOS, thyroid or iron for women.
No subscription or follow-up programme; every supply is a new order. Inconsistent site copy (discount codes, phone-consultation days).
A woman with several allergies can be left with only the £25 phone consultation and no explanation (runs/verify-w-combo3).
opportunities: Act on safety answers before payment (stop or switch on finasteride allergy, breast cancer, depression history) and explain why.
Offer a guided result with a reason ('this suits you because…') and an alternative when a product is removed.
Sell topical and combination options for men (topical finasteride, minoxidil, oral minoxidil under a prescriber).
A real women's pathway: differential questions (menopause, PCOS, iron, thyroid, post-partum) and prescription options such as oral minoxidil or spironolactone.
Subscription with check-ins and progress photos to support adherence over the 3 to 6 months finasteride needs.

verification.verdict: This report can be trusted for what it says about the anonymous part of the journey. Every baseline and all 11 high-consequence rules I re-tested came out the same as recorded, the product names, strengths and prices match the live pages, and every run folder cited exists. The main faults were labelling, not facts: 'flag-for-clinician' was claimed as observed when only 'no change' was seen, and a few options were filled in from the definition; these are now corrected or replayed. The report says nothing reliable about what the doctor does after payment, about age or sex handling, or about men who need to upload photos, and it is honest about that.
